claims.claim: Igneous rocks form when molten rock cools, crystallizes, and solidifies; molten material is magma beneath the surface and lava after it erupts at the surface.

Intrusive or plutonic igneous rocks solidify below the surface and usually cool slowly enough to form visible larger crystals, whereas extrusive or volcanic rocks cool at or near the surface and generally have smaller crystals or glassy material.
Igneous rocks are classified using chemical composition, mineral composition, texture, and structure.
A glassy volcanic texture records rapid cooling that leaves little time for crystals to develop; obsidian is an example of volcanic glass.
Vesicles are holes left by gas bubbles trapped during the cooling of lava.
Pyroclastic rocks are made of volcanic ash and other fragmented volcanic material erupted explosively.
Porphyritic texture can record larger crystals formed during earlier slow cooling that are later surrounded by a fine-grained or glassy groundmass after more rapid cooling.
